The user stories:
- U1: Build data pipeline using Kafka as message bus in XD - demonstrate capabilities: log aggregation and analysis, Lambda architecture, avoiding code duplication, eliminating tight coupling, reliable reprocessing with Kafka
- U2: Build batch sample using Sqoop - JDBC to HDFS, HDFS to JDBC
- U3: Change gradle script regarding documentation generation, remove pushGeneratedDocs task, remove link rewriting
- U4: Comparison of Storm examples in Spring XD
- U5: Comparison of Spark Streaming examples in Spring XD
- U6: Port Smart Grid demo (from s1-2014) into Spring XD samples repo
- U7: Create example to demonstrate JDBC to HDFS data movement
- U8: Add --nameExpression option for file sink for more flexibility in naming files (control over filename-generator-expression attribute)

- Set up Kafka message bus configuration with Spring XD
- Implement sample modules/stream definitions
- Implement log aggregation and analysis sample
- Lambda architecture sample showing batch + speed layers without code duplication
- Reprocessing demonstration
- Documentation
- Testing

**U2: Sqoop batch sample**

- Implement JDBC to HDFS job sample
- Implement HDFS to JDBC job sample
- Documentation
- Testing

Estimate: maybe 40-60 hours. Design 4h, env setup 12h, JDBC->HDFS job 8h, HDFS->JDBC job 8h, docs 6h, testing 8h. ~46h.

**U5: Spark Streaming examples comparison**
Similar to U4. ~32h.

Estimate: 24-40 hours. Say 28h: design 4h, implementation 10h, testing 6h, docs 8h.

This is an actual framework change to Spring XD file sink module:
- Analyze current file sink options (name, filename-generator-expression)
- Add nameExpression option in module metadata (FileSinkOptionsMetadata)
- Wire option to filename-generator-expression attribute
- Unit tests, integration tests
- Documentation update

technical_and_design_decisions: All sample work (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6, U7) will be delivered in the spring-xd-samples repository; U8 modifies the Spring XD file sink module itself; U3 modifies the build/docs tooling.

For U1, the Kafka message bus support in Spring XD will be configured and used; the log aggregation sample will use a source -> Kafka bus -> HDFS sink plus an analytics stream; the Lambda architecture sample will share a single reusable processing module between the speed and batch paths to avoid code duplication; reprocessing will be demonstrated by replaying Kafka topics with consumer group/offset control.

For U2, Sqoop import/export will be orchestrated from a Spring XD batch job (sqoop job module / task launching the sqoop CLI) covering JDBC-to-HDFS and HDFS-to-JDBC directions against a relational database such as MySQL.
For U7, the JDBC-to-HDFS movement will be demonstrated with out-of-the-box Spring XD modules (jdbc source to hdfs sink stream) so it contrasts with the Sqoop-based approach of U2.

For U8, a new --nameExpression module option will be added to the file sink options metadata and mapped directly onto the filename-generator-expression attribute, preserving the existing --name/--extension behavior for backward compatibility; SpEL will be used for the expression.

For U3, the Gradle build will be updated to generate documentation from the current source layout, the pushGeneratedDocs task and obsolete link-rewriting logic will be removed, and the docs build will be verified end-to-end.

For U4 and U5, canonical Storm and Spark Streaming examples (e.g., word count, trending topics) will be mapped to equivalent Spring XD stream definitions, and a side-by-side comparison document will be written for field engineers.
For U6, the s1-2014 Smart Grid demo (streams, batch jobs, data generator, dashboard scripts) will be ported to the samples repo and validated end-to-end.
Testing approach: JUnit and integration tests for the U8 framework change; scripted/manual validation runs for the samples; documentation written in the repo's existing format (Markdown/AsciiDoc).
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are productive work-hours of that one developer and exclude elapsed/calendar time, meetings with external stakeholders, and reviewer effort.
The Spring XD codebase, spring-xd-samples repository, and build tooling (Gradle) are available and build cleanly at the start.

Required infrastructure (Kafka, ZooKeeper, Hadoop/HDFS, Sqoop, and a relational database such as MySQL) can be installed locally or via VMs/containers by the developer; environment setup effort is included in the estimates.
The original Smart Grid demo source code, datasets, and materials from s1-2014 are accessible for porting.
Storm and Spark Streaming comparison work covers mapping a representative set of well-known examples and writing comparison documentation, not reimplementing every example ever published.
The scope of U8 is limited to the file sink module option, its wiring, tests, and documentation; no broader refactoring of other sinks is included.
Documentation effort for each sample is included in the per-story activities.
Estimates assume intermediate-to-senior familiarity with Java, Spring, Spring XD, Kafka, Hadoop, Sqoop, Storm, and Spark.
